audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Malta, viper, Publius healings, voyage to Rome, Roman Judean leaders, Isaiah hearing text, final bold unhindered proclamation.

verses.restored: When we had been brought safely through, then we learned that the island was called Malta.

familiar.text: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.

verses.restored: The islanders showed us no ordinary kindness; kindling a fire, they welcomed us all because of the rain that had set in and because of the cold.

familiar.text: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

verses.restored: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks and placed it on the fire; a viper came out from the heat and fastened on his hand.

familiar.text: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

verses.restored: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they were saying to one another, Surely this human is a murderer, whom, though saved/healed from the sea, Justice has not allowed to live.

familiar.text: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.

verses.restored: But he shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no harm.

familiar.text: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.

verses.restored: They were expecting him to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing out of place happening to him, changing their minds, they said he was a god.

familiar.text: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

verses.restored: Now in the places around that site were lands belonging to the first man of the island, named Publius, who received us and hosted us kindly three days.

familiar.text: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

verses.restored: It happened that the father of Publius was lying down, afflicted with fevers and dysentery. Paul went in to him, prayed, laid hands on him, and healed him.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.

verses.restored: When this happened, the rest of those on the island who had weaknesses also came and were being healed.

familiar.text: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:

verses.restored: They honored us with many honors, and when we were putting out to sea, they put on board the things we needed.

familiar.text: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.

verses.restored: After three months we put out to sea in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered on the island, whose sign was the Twin Brothers.

familiar.text: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

verses.restored: Putting in at Syracuse, we remained three days.

familiar.text: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.

verses.restored: From there, making a circuit, we arrived at Rhegium; after one day a south wind came up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.

familiar.text: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:

verses.restored: There, finding siblings, we were invited to remain with them seven days. And so we came to Rome.

familiar.text: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.

verses.restored: From there the siblings, hearing the things concerning us, came to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. Seeing them, Paul gave thanks to the Divine and took courage.

familiar.text: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.

verses.restored: When we entered Rome, Paul was permitted to remain by himself with the soldier guarding him.

familiar.text: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.

verses.restored: After three days he called together those who were first among the Judeans. When they had gathered, he said to them, Men, siblings, though I had done nothing against the people or ancestral customs, I was handed over as prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

verses.restored: After examining me, they wished to release me because there was no cause of death in me.

familiar.text: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.

verses.restored: But when the Judeans spoke against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, not as though having anything to accuse my nation of.

familiar.text: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.

verses.restored: Because of this cause therefore I called you to see and speak with you, for because of the hope of Israel I am wearing this chain.

familiar.text: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

verses.restored: They said to him, We have neither received letters about you from Judea, nor has any of the siblings arriving reported or spoken anything harmful concerning you.

familiar.text: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.

verses.restored: But we consider it worthy to hear from you what you think, for concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.

familiar.text: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.

verses.restored: Arranging a day with him, many came to him at the lodging, to whom he explained, bearing witness to the reign of the Divine and persuading them concerning Jesus from both the Law of Moses and the Prophets, from morning until evening.

familiar.text: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.

verses.restored: Some were persuaded by the things spoken, but others were not trusting.

familiar.text: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.

verses.restored: Being discordant with one another, they departed after Paul said one word: Beautifully/well did the holy Spirit speak through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,

familiar.text: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,

verses.restored: saying, Go to this people and say, Hearing you will hear and certainly not understand, and seeing you will see and certainly not perceive.

familiar.text: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:

verses.restored: For the heart of this people has grown thick, and with the ears they heard heavily, and their eyes they closed, lest they should see with the eyes and hear with the ears and understand with the heart and turn, and I would heal them.

familiar.text: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

verses.restored: Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation/healing of the Divine has been sent to the nations; they also will hear.

familiar.text: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.

verses.restored: [Some later manuscripts add that after he said these things, the Judeans departed, having much dispute among themselves.]

familiar.text: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

verses.restored: He remained two whole years in his own rented lodging and welcomed all those coming to him,

familiar.text: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,

verses.restored: proclaiming the reign of the Divine and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Messiah with all boldness, unhindered.

familiar.text: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
